utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-79-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Registrar, and good afternoon to you, too. Mr. Stanisic, before I proceed any further, I want to make sure that what I am saying in English and all the rest of the proceedings today are being received by you in a language that you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may sit down. Thank you. Could I have appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Mark Harmon. Appearing with me is Ms. Anna Richterova, and the case manager, Salla Moilanen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good afternoon to you and your team. Mr. Stanisic, I am informed that you have expressed your wish to this Tribunal that for the purpose of this Initial Appearance you would like to represent yourself, in other words, that you do not wish to be assisted by counsel today. Do I have the right -- the correct information?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. We'll come to the question of counsel and representation later on. You may sit down. Also, before we proceed and go to the substance of this Initial Appearance, it is my duty could I to bring to your attention, Mr. Stanisic, the right you have to remain silent. This right you enjoy under our Statute but also under our Rules of Evidence and Procedure, and basically it means that no one can force you to say anything, to answer any questions, and this applies from the beginning of the proceedings until they are over, that is, not only today but later on as we proceed in -- with the pre-trial stage and subsequently with the trial itself. This right to remain silent arises, actually, out of a broader right that you have against self-incrimination, and that right you enjoy throughout the entire proceedings. I will start by giving some details on the indictment that is -- exists against you, for your sake, in case you have some -- some information that you haven't got right, but also for the sake of the public. I wish to inform you, Mr. Stanisic, that you are the only accused in the indictment which carries case number IT-04-79-I, and that this indictment was confirmed by my colleague, Judge El Mahdi, on the 25th of February of this year. Subsequently the indictment was made public following a decision reached by the same Judge, by Judge El Mahdi on the 10th of March, 2005. I am informed that you, Mr. Stanisic, turned yourself in and therefore surrendered yourself into the custody of this Tribunal and that in fact you arrived at the seat of this Tribunal here in The Hague last week precisely on the 11th of March, 2005. I will proceed with a summary of the indictment that the Prosecution has brought against you and which has been confirmed by this Tribunal. According to the indictment, as from the 21st of December of 1991, you were minister without portfolio in the council of ministers which was set up by the Assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The indictment also alleges that from the 1st of April, 1992, you were the minister of interior of the newly established Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs, BiH. In this position, according to the indictment, you were the highest authority in the MUP. Your official responsibility included public and state security. According to the Prosecutor, you had overall authority and responsibility for the functioning of the police forces within Republika Srpska and that all commanders of the security services centres were directly subordinated to you. This indictment charges you with criminal responsibility under two categories. The first one is individual criminal responsibility grounded -- based on Article 7(1) of the Statute. You are in fact charged in the indictment on the basis of your individual criminal responsibility pursuant to the said Article for alleged crimes which are referred to in Articles 3 and 5 of the Statute of this Tribunal, which according to the Prosecutor you are alleged to have committed, instigated, or in whose planning, preparation, and execution you are said to have aided and abetted. By using the word "committed" in this indictment, the Prosecutor is not alleging that you personally committed any of the crimes charged. "Committed" in the indictment includes participation in a joint criminal enterprise. Coming to the joint criminal enterprise alleged and mentioned in the indictment, according to the Prosecutor this came into existence no later than the establishment of the Assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 24th of October, 1991, and continued throughout the period of the conflict in BiH until the signing of the Dayton Accords in 1995. According to the Prosecutor, the objective of the joint criminal enterprise was to permanently remove and ethnically cleanse by force or other illegal means Bosnian Muslims, Bosnian Croats, and other non-Serbs from the territory of the planned Serbian state by the commission of the crimes alleged in the indictment. According to the indictment, you, Mr. Stanisic, are said to have participated in the joint criminal enterprise as a co-perpetrator from no later than April 1, 1992, until at least the 31st of December, 1992, by commanding and directing members and agents of the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the MUP, Republika Srpska MUP, who were engaged in implementing the answer engagement of the joint criminal enterprise or who participated in the perpetration of the crimes listed in the indictment. Also by encouraging and facilitating and thus instigating the commission of crimes against Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims, and other non-Serbs by not taking any active steps to investigate, arrest, and/or punish the perpetrators of such crimes. The indictment alleges that several persons, individuals, participated in this joint criminal enterprise, and according to the indictment, each participant by acts of commission or acts of omission contributed to achieving the overall objective of the enterprise. The indictment alleges that you, Mr. Stanisic, worked in concert with other members of the joint criminal enterprise amongst whom there were the following: Stojan Zupljanin, Radoslav Brdjanin, the late General Momir Talic, Slobodan Dubocanin, also deceased, Simo Drljaca, also deceased, Darko Mrdja, Ljuban Ecim, General Ratko Mladic, Radovan Karadzic, Nikola Koljevic, who is also deceased, Momcilo Krajisnik, Biljana Plavsic, and other members of the Bosnian Serb leadership and of the Serbian Democratic Party, the SDS, at the republic, regional, and municipal levels. The Prosecution also alleges that included in this joint criminal enterprise were also members of the civilian bodies within Bosnia and Herzegovina, including regional and municipal crisis staffs, members of the Yugoslav People's Army, the JNA, the Yugoslav army, the VJ, the army of Republika Srpska, the VRS, the Territorial Defence, the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the MUP, the Serbian MUP, and members of Serb and Bosnian Serb paramilitary forces and volunteer units, as well as military and political figures from the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. That's as far as responsibility, individual criminal responsibility under 7(1) is concerned. I'm going into these details particularly since you decided to represent yourself, because if you had a lawyer here, it would have been a little bit easier for me. But as I tried to explain earlier on, you are also charged with criminal responsibility that we refer to as superior command responsibility, and this is brought against you in terms of Article 7(3) of the Statute. Basically what this means is that in real terms, the indictment alleges that you, while holding the position of -- a position of superior authority, you are also individually criminally responsible for the acts or omissions of your subordinates pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Statute. The allegation against you is that your -- in your capacity as minister of the interior, you exercised de jure and de facto command and control over the police forces that participated in the crimes alleged in the indictment. According to the indictment, you knew or had reason to know that crimes -- that the crimes alleged in the indictment were about to be committed or had been committed by your subordinates and that you failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such acts or to punish the perpetrators thereof. According to the indictment, your duty included an obligation to investigate and establish the facts of the crimes that were committed, to put an end to criminal activity, to impose appropriate punitive measures on the perpetrators, and to take the appropriate measures to prevent or deter further criminal acts committed by your subordinates. I will now proceed to give some information as to the underlying crimes in this indictment of -- in this indictment, the crimes that are being charged against you or brought against you. According to the indictment, between the 1st of April, 1992, and 31st December, 1992, you are said to have committed the following crimes, and I'm going through them one by one: The first one is persecution. Persecution on political, racial, or religious grounds of the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat populations in the areas designated as the Serbian autonomous regions including the municipalities of Prijedor, Kotor Varos, Sanski Most, Kljuc, Teslic, Donji Vakuf, and Banja Luka in the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and further in the municipalities of Bileca, Bosanski Samac, Brcko, Doboj, Gacko, Ilijas, Pale, Vlasenica, Visegrad, Vogosca and Zvornik. The indictment alleges that Bosnian Serb forces under your command and control committed persecution in the Autonomous Region of Krajina and the other municipalities that I have just mentioned upon or against the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat population. According to the Prosecution, this persecution included the killing of Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats during and after attacks on villages and non-Serb areas during deportation and forcible transfer. Second, killings related to detention facilities or committed during transfer to or out of detention facilities that are mentioned in the indictment. Cruel or inhumane treatment during and after attacks on towns and villages and during deportation and forcible transfer including torture, physical and psychological abuse, sexual violence, and forced existence under inhumane living conditions. More: Cruel or inhumane treatment in detention facilities. This inhumane treatment included beatings, torture, physical and psychological abuse, sexual violence, and humiliation. (e), unlawful detention in detention facilities. (f), the establishment and person pet situation of inhumane living conditions in detention facilities. These conditions included the failure to provide adequate accommodation or shelter, food or water, medical care and hygienic sanitation facilities. (g), forcible transfer and transportation. (h), the appropriation or plunder of property during and after attacks in detention facilities and in the course of deportations or forcible transfers. The appropriation of property included the practice of forcing Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats to sign documents transferring the title to their real and personal property to Bosnian Serb governmental authorities in order to be able to -- in order to be allowed to leave the Autonomous Region of Krajina and the other municipalities that I mentioned earlier. Under the heading of persecution also the Prosecution alleges that you are criminally responsible for the wanton destruction of Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat villages and areas, including the destruction of religious and cultural buildings and the looting of residential and commercial property. And finally under the heading of persecution, you are charged with the imposition and maintenance of restrictive and discriminatory measures including the denial of freedom of movement, the denial of employment through removal from positions of authority in local government institutions, the military and the police, and general dismissal from employment. Also, the invasion of privacy through arbitrary searches of houses, the denial of the right to judicial process and the denial of equal access to public services. That accounts for the charge and the counts that cover the crime of persecution. But you are also charged with the crime of extermination and murder. The indictment indeed further alleges that in the same period that I mentioned earlier, you committed the crime of extermination and murder of Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats in the Autonomous Region of Krajina and the other municipalities that I mentioned earlier. The extermination and murder were effected by killings committed during and after attacks on towns and villages, in detention facilities, and during deportations or forcible transfers. The next crime that you are charged with is one of torture, cruel treatment, and inhumane acts. The indictment indeed further alleges that in the same time period you committed the crime of inhumane acts inflicted on the non-Serb population in the Autonomous Region of Krajina and the other municipalities that I mentioned earlier. Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats, according to the Prosecutor, were confined in inhumane conditions and subjected to intentional infliction of severe pain or suffering by beatings, torture, sexual violence, humiliation, harassment, and psychological abuses in camps, police stations, military barracks, and other detention facilities as well as during and after attacks on villages and during forcible transfers and deportations. The last category of crimes that you are charged with can be described as deportation and other inhumane acts, but to be precise, the indictment alleges that in the same time period, you committed the crime of unlawful forcible transfer and deportation of tens of thousands of Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats from the Autonomous Region of Krajina and the other municipalities that I mentioned earlier. In order to achieve this objective, Bosnian Serb forces, including the police forces of the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs in BiH, which was under the effective control -- which was under your effective control or of that of other members of the joint criminal enterprise, you subjugated villages and towns in Bosnia and Herzegovina and participated with members of the SDS, the Serbian Democratic Party, in the disarming of the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat population. The indictment alleges that the towns and villages, including areas in which the inhabitants complied and offered no resistance, were then attacked. These attacks were intended to compel the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat population to flee. After taking control of the towns and villages, according to the indictment, the Bosnian Serb forces often rounded up the remaining Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat population and forcibly removed them from the area. On other occasions, the Bosnian Serb forces, in cooperation with the local Bosnian Serb authorities, imposed restrictive and discriminatory measures on the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat population and engaged in a campaign of terror designed to drive them out of the territory. The majority of the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat population that remained was eventually deported or forcibly transferred from their homes. Now, the President of this Tribunal, on the 11th of March, 2005, issued an order assigning your case, this case, to Trial Chamber II, of which I am the President. Subsequently, on the 14th of March, 2005, I, in my capacity as Presiding Judge of Trial Chamber II, designated myself as the Pre-Trial Judge for the purpose -- purposes of today's Initial Appearance. I told you in the beginning that although you have chosen to represent yourself today during this Initial Appearance, it is my responsibility as the Pre-Trial Judge doing the Initial Appearance to give you all the information that is necessary to put you in a position where you would know what your rights are when it comes to legal representation. Of course there is no doubt at all, and I want -- wish to confirm this to you, that you have a right to defend yourself. You have a right to represent yourself today in this Initial Appearance, and you have also got a protected right to defend yourself later on when it comes to the pre-trial stage and also the trial. But you also have a right to be assisted by a counsel of your own choosing. However, in this respect, it is my responsibility to make it clear that the right to have -- of accused to have a counsel of his own choosing is not an absolute one, and it is regulated by various directives and orders, also by the Rules of Evidence and Procedure. The responsibility and discretion belongs to the Registrar of this Tribunal. Of course the Trial Chamber will intervene if your being interfered with. As long as the discretion exercised by the Registrar is reasonably exercised, the Trial Chamber will not intervene. The Statute as well as the Rules also provide for legal aid should you qualify to it. In other words, within the general umbrella of your having a right to be assisted by counsel of your own choosing, if you satisfy the conditions that are laid down by the various instruments of -- and Rules of this Tribunal, then in terms of Rule 45(A), you have a right to ask to be assigned counsel. That counsel will be assigned in accordance with the procedure established in an ad hoc directive. I do not intend to say much more on this. I think from what I can see, you are understanding me perfectly well. If you have any questions in this regard, please stand up and speak now. My suggestion to you is that you immediately, now that you are here in The Hague, take this matter up with the representatives of the Registrar so that you know what your position is. I now come to the next stage, and I am tasked by the Rules of this Tribunal to establish that indeed you are the Mr. Stanisic that was indicted by this Tribunal. In due course, then, I will come to the most important part of today's Initial Appearance, but for the time being could you please stand up. For the time being, I'm going to ask you a few questions. Could you please give me your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a question. If you prefer not to answer it, you have every right not to answer it. Do you have any nicknames? Are you known by any nicknames?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no nickname, nor have I ever had one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. What is your date of birth? When were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 30th of June, 1954.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And where were you born, your place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ponor, Pale municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what is your present nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the citizenship of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And now I'm going to ask you for your last address, but I don't think this is of any interest to the public, so we'll go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Registrar. Are your -- are the members of your family, all the members of your family aware that you are presently here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everyone knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the -- would you like me to inform anyone amongst your relatives about your presence here in The Hague and your state of detention here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do I also take it that your embassy, the embassy of Serbia here in The Hague is aware of your transfer and presence -- state of detention here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, you don't need me to contact the embassy of Serbia and inform them of anything?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Mr. Stanisic, I'm sure you are aware of this, but our Statute on our Rules ensure that the -- every accused here enjoys a certain number of rights. These rights are essentially enshrined in Articles 20 and 21 of our Statute. You also have a reflection of them in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and these are internationally recognised rights. So as to make sure you are aware of these rights, I'm going to ask now Madam Registrar to read out loud Articles 20 and 21 of our Statute, and then I will ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Article 20: "Commencement of trial proceedings. The Trial Chamber should ensure that a trial is fair and expeditious and that proceedings are conducted in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence with full respect for the rights of the accused and due regard for the protection of victims and witnesses. A person against whom an indictment has been confirmed shall, pursuant to an order or an arrest warrant of the International Tribunal, be taken into custody immediately informed of the charges against him and transferred to the International Tribunal. The Trial Chamber shall read the indictment, satisfy itself that the rights of the accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment and instruct the accused to enter a plea. The Trial Chamber should then set a date for trial. The hearings should be public unless the Trial Chamber decides to close the proceedings in accordance with its Rules of Procedure and Evidence." Article 21: "Rights of the accused. "All persons shall be equal between the International Tribunal. "In the determination of charges against him, the accused shall be entitled to a fair and public hearing subject to Article 22 of the Statute. "The accused should be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to the provisions of the present Statute. "In the determination of any charge against the accused pursuant to the present Statute, the accused shall be entitled to the follow minimum guarantees in full equality. "(a). To be informed promptly and in detail in a language which he understands of the nature and cause of the charge against him. "(b) to have adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his defence and to communicate with counsel of his own choosing. "(c) to be tried without undue delay. "(d) to be tried in his presence and defend himself in person or threw legal assistance of his own choosing. To be informed if he does not have legal assistance of this right and to have legal assistance assigned to him in any case where the interests of justice so require and without payment by him in any such case if he does not have sufficient means to pay for it. "(e) to examine or have examined the witnesses against him and to obtain the attendance and examination of witnesses on his behalf under the same conditions as witnesses against him. "(f) to have the free assistant of an interpreter if he cannot understand or speak the language used in the International Tribunal. "(g) not to compel to testify against himself or to confess guilt." Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Stanisic, do you understand the importance of these rights contained in these two articles that Madam Registrar has just read?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you been served with a -- with a copy of the indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you understood it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you have understood exactly what you are being charged with.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want me to read out the indictment in full? According to the Rules I'm supposed now to proceed with the reading of the indictment in full. But you also have a right to waive that, in which we will proceed with the next stage of the Initial Appearance. My question to you is: Do you wish to have the indictment against you read out in full, or do you waive that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Now, while you're still standing up, I'll explain to you what the next stage is. The next stage is I'm now going to proceed with asking you whether you wish to enter a plea to the various counts contained in the indictment today, or whether, in case you wish to enter a plea today, whether you will be pleading guilty or not guilty to any or all of the counts that are brought against you. That's the procedure basically that we will be following. However, I need to explain to you that our Rules do not require you necessarily to enter a plea today. You may choose not to enter a plea today, but then you have 30 days within which you can enter a plea, and our Rules also provide that if within those 30 days you do not enter a plea, then I will enter a plea on your of what and that will be a plea of not guilty. So that's the position. Mr. Stanisic, are you ready and willing to enter a plea to the charges that are brought against you, to the counts that are brought against you in this indictment today, or do you wish to delay your entering of the plea?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am ready to enter a plea today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So the way I will go about it is as follows: I will tell you under which count what you are being charged with, the information I gave already in the explanatory part. And then at the end I will explain how you wish to plead to those counts one by one. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's start with the first count, Mr. Stanisic. The first count contained in the indictment is one of persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, this being a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(h) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this first count, guilty or not guilty? Incidentally, you are being charged both under Article 7(1) and Article 7(3), that is, individual criminal responsibility and superior command possibility. How do you wish to plead to this first count, guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I come to the second count which is brought against you, and this is a charge of extermination, being a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(b) of this Statute and once more you are being charged both under Article 7(1) and under Article 7(3) of the Statute of this Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this second -- second count which is one of extermination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The third count against you is one of murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(a) of the Statute of this Tribunal, and once more you are being charged both under 7(1) and under 7(3) of the Statute of this Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this third count, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the fourth count is one of murder, this time being a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Common Article 3, 1 of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Once more, you're being charged both under 7(1) and under 7(3) of the Statute of this Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this fourth count, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the fifth count is one of torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(f) of the Statute of this Tribunal, and once more, the Prosecution -- the indictment alleges that you are responsible both under 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of this Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this fifth count, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the sixth count against you is one of torture. This time it is alleged as a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, and which is punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Again, 7 -- Articles 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute are being invoked against you. How do you wish to plead to this sixth count of torture, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the seventh count you are being charged with, cruel treatment, it being a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Common Article 3, 1 of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 and which is punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. Once more, Articles 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute are being invoked against you. How do you wish to plead to this seventh count of cruel treatment, guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the eighth count against you, Mr. Stanisic, is a charge of inhumane acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(i) of the Statute of this Tribunal, and again Articles 7(1) and 7(3) are being -- of the Statute are being invoked against you. How do you wish to plead to this eighth count, that is one of a charge of inhumane acts, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the ninth count the Prosecution alleges against you -- brings against you, a charge of deportation, it being a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(d) of the Statute of this Tribunal. Again, Articles 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute are invoked against you. How do you wish to plead to this ninth count, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And in the tenth count, you are being charged with inhumane acts, namely forcible transfer, which is a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(i) of the Statute of this Tribunal, which Articles 7(1) and 7(3) being invoked also here. How do you wish to plead to this tenth count which is brought -- that is brought against you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Please take a seat, Mr. Stanisic. Madam Registrar, I would like to record that the accused entered a plea of not guilty to each of the ten counts brought against him in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Stanisic, I need to also inform you that in case you change your mind in due course, that you can always change your plea, and you can change your plea with regard to the entire indictment, and you can change your plea with regard to one or more of the counts that I referred to and which are brought -- which are brought against you in the indictment. There is an important matter that I need to make myself clear about, because this is of great interest to you as a new detainee here in Scheveningen. You are now under the custody of the Tribunal. The Initial Appearance has taken place, and Rule 63 of our Rules of Evidence and Procedure provides that questioning by the Prosecutor of an accused, including after the Initial Appearance, shall not proceed without the presence of counsel unless the accused has voluntarily and expressly agreed to proceed without counsel present. If the accused subsequently expresses a desire to have counsel, questioning shall thereupon cease, stop, and shall only resume when the accused's counsel is present. The questioning, including any waiver of the right to counsel shall be audio recorded or video recorded in accordance with the procedure provided for in Rule 43, which I don't need to read out to you, "and the Prosecutor shall at the beginning of the questioning caution the accused in accordance with Rule 42(A)(iii)." Basically the Prosecutor would need to caution you that you have the right to remain silent and anything that you might say would be -- could or would be used in testimony against you. Or could be used in testimony. So I have read out Rule 63 to you, even though for the time being you've told me that you don't wish not to be represented by the counsel, but these are your rights, and I want to make sure that you are made aware of them. In the next couple of days, I will proceed with appointing a Pre-Trial Judge. This Judge will look after the pre-trial stage on behalf of the Trial Chamber, and he will have the task of summoning periodically a so-called Status Conference. According to our Rules, a Status Conference has to be held, convened, within 120 days -- the first one within 120 days as from today. The subsequent ones within 120 days each from the previous Status Conference. The purpose of a Status Conference is twofold. First, it allows for the parties and the Trial Chamber to organise exchanges between the parties so to ensure -- so as to ensure the expeditious -- an expeditious preparation for trial, also to ensure that all the disclosure obligations, particularly on the Prosecution, are being observed. Secondly, the Pre-Trial Judge will also and in addition have the opportunity of seeing you in person and ensure that -- first, that you are being treated well, listen to any remarks or complaints or questions that you might have, and take all the necessary action that might become necessary, if at all. Later on, you, or if you will have counsel later on, your counsel, will be informed of the date of the first of these Status Conferences, and of course later on you will be informed as we go along. In the meantime, I have signed an order, which I am sure you are aware of, keeping you in custody here in Scheveningen. But it is also my duty to inform you that pursuant to Rule 65 of our Rules of Evidence and Procedure, you have a right to file an application for provisional release. The fact that you are not represented by counsel is of no impediment, no obstacle. You can find it -- file it yourself or it can be filed later on by your counsel, if you have one, and it will be -- it will be given all due attention by the Trial Chamber collectively and not by the Pre-Trial Judge. I'm mentioning this also because should you decide to apply for counsel, for legal assistance, and should this take more time than you expect and in the meantime you would like to file an application for provisional release, you have every right to file it. It doesn't mean to say that you will get provisional release, but you have every right to file it. So the only other thing, I tell you about is that if you have difficulties, I'm sure that you can ask for assistance -- the Detention Unit. And any such application that you may wish to file will be filed in your name. I turn over to you, Mr. Harmon. I think -- I barely need to remind you of your responsibilities and obligations under Rule 66(A)(i). Would I like to remind you that pursuant to this sub-rule, within 30 days of today's Initial Appearance you need to make available to the accused, if he continues to represent himself, or to his counsel if he has one, in a language in which the accused understands all the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought. I am pretty sure that you are aware of this right -- of this obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour may be absolutely confident that we will comply with that Rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And now I turn on again to you, Mr. Stanisic. We have also Rule 72, and in particular I'm referring you to paragraph (A) of Rule 72, pursuant to which you will have a 30-day period for filing any preliminary motions once you have received the supporting material in your own language that is due to you under Rule 66 that I mentioned a couple of seconds ago. By "preliminary motions," I mean the motions that are listed in Rule 72, and which include also motions challenging the jurisdiction of the Tribunal or alleging defects in the form of the indictment. Incidentally, I might as well ask you whether you have already available a copy of the Rules of Evidence and Procedure in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So you can refer to Rule 72. We are almost finished. Mr. Harmon, is there any matter that the Prosecution wishes to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There is none, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Harmon. Mr. Stanisic, is there any matter that you would -- that you wish to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing. But, Your Honour, all I would like to say is that I came here voluntarily in order to establish the truth before this Honourable Chamber, and that is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. I want to make sure also that since your decision to surrender to this Tribunal voluntarily that you have been treated well. Have you been treated well?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And you have no special concerns as relates to your state of detention or your health that you would like to make me aware of? If necessary, we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have nothing to complain about. All I want to do is to establish the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. Last thing before we rise is I will also instruct the Registrar to start the ball rolling with a view to also fixing a date for the -- for this trial. I think it's almost superfluous on my part to explain that that is not going to happen overnight. It will take it's time, but I will be giving instructions to the Registrar not to sleep on this matter but to give it the utmost attention, Mr. Stanisic. I thank you. You may sit down. We stand adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Initial Appearance adjourned at
